Subject: PeakSpin launch: surge causing elevated 5xx/429s — urgent

Karthik,

We're in the middle of the phased launch for feature flag rollout and hit a big problem starting ~08:00 PT. We're seeing a steady rise in 429s and 5xx responses from the Redwood endpoint. Clients are timing out and retrying aggressively which looks like a retry storm — errors spike then a flood of retries. Attached is a short CSV with sample request/response rows and timestamps (peakspin_error_log_snippet.csv).

This is impacting our core search route; latency has jumped from ~80ms to 2–3s for some requests and overall throughput fell through the floor. We paused traffic for now but need immediate guidance: are you seeing throttles on your side? Is this a configuration issue on PeakSpin's ramp?

Can you escalate to engineering? Marcus (cc'd) is our infra lead. We need a quick remediation plan and whether Redwood can temporarily increase capacity for the next hour while we stabilize.

Thanks — Sara

Subject: Re: PeakSpin launch: surge causing elevated 5xx/429s — urgent

Quick engineering summary from the serving side (what we observed 07:55–08:15 PT):
- Excessive retry traffic from a subset of client IPs; retries had low/no jitter and 0–50ms initial backoff which amplified load.
- Global per-model token QPS threshold was hit; our in-service rate limiter returned 429s and a subset of overloaded nodes returned 5xx as connection queues overflowed.
- The host-level autoscaler wasn't triggered fast enough due to short sustained window and our conservative cooldowns.

Immediate actions taken (08:10–08:40):
- Enabled temporary soft-reject policy (503/429 with Retry-After) and ramped per-customer QPS cap for PeakSpin by 2.5x on the affected model variant.
- Triggered accelerated autoscale on the dedicated pool for the tenant (warm nodes from standby).
- Tuned global sequencer backpressure thresholds to shed the heaviest tails.
- Pushed short-term config to edge rate-limiter to prioritize tail latency and avoid connection queue saturation.

Suggested customer-side changes (to implement now):
1) Client SDK: implement exponential backoff with full-jitter, initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=10s.
2) Ramp guidance: avoid step increases larger than +20r/s per minute for each concurrency shard. Preferred: linear ramp of +5–10r/s per minute per shard.
3) If possible, shift non-critical traffic to off-peak / lower-priority model variant during the ramp.

I've attached the metrics slice for 08:00–08:12 showing QPS, 429/5xx rates, and node saturation (redwood_metrics_2026-07-12-08-00-12-00.png).

We'll continue to monitor — I'll keep this thread updated.

Dylan Brooks

Subject: Update & recommended ramp playbook — PeakSpin launch

Sara / Marcus — 

Status update and concrete next steps:
- Mitigations applied: temporary per-customer QPS increase, accelerated autoscale, and rate-limiter shaping to reduce connection queueing. Result: 429/5xx rates dropped to baseline within ~18 minutes after our changes.
- Short-term ask: please implement the SDK backoff settings Dylan recommended and cut the next ramp step in half while we run a controlled test.

Recommended ramp playbook (attached ramp_playbook_v1.pdf):
- Phase 0 (canary): 5r/s for 2 minutes; validate P95 latency and 429s
- Phase 1: +10r/s/min until 50r/s (per shard) with client-side jitter/backoff
- Phase 2: Hold for 10 minutes, run traffic mix test, then continue linear ramp

We're also offering a one-time usage credit to offset the impacted requests during the incident — I'll coordinate with our billing team and confirm in the next hour. Evelyn, please own the credit confirmation and follow-up.

We'll set up a 30-min postmortem call this afternoon to walk through root cause and longer-term controls (better autoscale tuning, early retry detection, automated ramp safety gates). When would you prefer to meet?

Apologies again for the disruption — we recognize this is poorly timed during your launch and are prioritizing remedies.

Thanks,
